description: Verifies the seal of a run. Short form, which needs only what is short: request is the run_trajectory request as it was sent, with its readout and its from, whose request has none, when it had them (the answer's inputs holds neither), and run_seal is the seal its answer gave. The run is computed again, under a physics permit and the limits and refusals of run_trajectory, and the answer is holds (the seal given is the seal the request runs to), cause ("run_seal" when it is not), recomputed_run_seal and recomputed_receipt_sha384 when it holds (else no seal: run_trajectory gives the true one), compared, and text_not_compared: no answer text the agent holds is compared. Long form: the whole run_trajectory answer sent back as it came, without request. Its state digest and run seal are recomputed from its exact hex values, then its request is computed again under a physics permit and the engine's answer compared with it, value by value and byte for byte, receipt included: holds is true only when every byte is the engine's, values_hold when every value is, else cause names the seal, load_signature (a signed load that does not verify), answer_text (with differs_at, the first field that differs) or engine_version (an answer of another version). A chain is verified by its request with from, run_seal and chain_seal, or by links, its answers in order, each computed again from the links before it; a chained answer alone is refused (AnswerCarriesNoRequest). Nothing is stored, so each form answers the same on every connection. On this open connection one address holds at most 1 physics permit at a time, and long work (a solve, a plan of runs or of solves, a run of more than 10000 steps, or a verification that computes one again) runs 1 at a time. A call that finds no permit or no place is answered "Too many concurrent physics tasks." and nothing waits: the same call sent later is answered once one is free. An answer is waited for 60 seconds, and long work is stopped there.

inputSchema.description: Either request and run_seal alone, the short form: the run is computed again and its seal compared with run_seal. Or the whole run_trajectory answer sent back as it was returned, without request, the long form: inputs, frames, outcome, steps_landed, reject, run_seal, final_state, final_residual_conservation_error_hex, max_residual_conservation_error_hex and state_digest are then all required, along with the rest of the answer. The trajectory chain, the state digest and the run seal are recomputed from its exact hex values; then its request is computed again under a physics permit and the limits of run_trajectory, and the engine's whole answer to it compared with the answer sent, value by value and then byte for byte, the receipt included, so an answer that holds is every byte the engine's. A seal has no key: an answer whose values were rewritten with its seals worked out again holds every seal, and only the computation shows it is not the engine's. An answer that continues a sealed upstream run (its chain names upstream_run_seal) carries the upstream's seal and not its request, and its long form is refused (AnswerCarriesNoRequest): its chain's answers in order, as links, carry each request, and each link is computed again from the links before it. Or links alone: a chain's answers in order, held as the long form holds one. A design_run answer sent whole is designed again and held the same way. The long form's answer carries holds, true when the answer sent is every byte the engine's, and values_hold beside it, true when every value of it is the engine's answer to its request computed again, whatever its spelling: each number by its 64-bit value, strings, flags and null exactly, keys and their order, the receipt string among them. A copy whose numbers a client wrote again in its own spelling (0.0001 for 1.0e-4, 12 for 12.0) has holds false and values_hold true, and differs_at names the first place its text differs. An answer the engine signed (signature, ML-DSA-87 over its receipt, with issued_at, expires_at and nonce) has its signature checked first, against public_key or else this engine's own key: one that does not hold is cause signature, named (SignatureDoesNotVerify, SignatureExpired, SignatureNonceReplayed, SignatureKeyMismatch, ReceiptDoesNotMatch, SignatureAbsent when public_key is given and there is none), and nothing is computed.

chain_seal.description: With request and run_seal: a chained answer's chain_seal.

inputs.description: The inputs of the run_trajectory answer, sent back as returned: the request that was run. It is hashed, and run again, with the answer's readout when it has one, under a physics permit and the limits of run_trajectory. A card's fields, units and bounds are in describe_card.

links.description: Alone: a chain's answers in order.

public_key.description: The base64 of the ML-DSA-87 public key (2,592 bytes) to check the answer's signature with; without it, this engine's own.

request.description: With run_seal alone: the run_trajectory request as it was sent, with its readout and its from when it had them (the answer's inputs holds neither; the upstream request in that from goes without a readout, as run_trajectory took it). It is run again, under a physics permit and the limits of run_trajectory, and its seal is compared with run_seal. Its fields are run_trajectory's. Worked example of the short form, as the whole arguments: {"request":{"domain":"energy","card":"thermal","initial":{"temperature_k":293.15},"dt_s":1.0,"segments":[{"steps":60,"load":{"heat_power_w":5.0,"ambient_k":293.15}}],"record_every":60},"run_seal":"<the run_seal of its run_trajectory answer, 96 lowercase hex digits>"}.

run_seal.description: The run_seal of the run_trajectory answer: with request, or as part of the whole answer.

seen_nonces.description: Nonces of signatures already seen: one of them again is SignatureNonceReplayed.
